title: This week in recruiting tools: Juicebox buys Fetcher, LinkedIn Hiring Assistant inside iCIMS, Workday ships Candidate Profile and agents
summary: A consolidation week across the recruiting stack: Juicebox agreed to acquire Fetcher's assets, iCIMS wired in LinkedIn's Hiring Assistant, Metaview went deeper into Workday, Workday launched Candidate Profile plus HR agents, Eightfold appointed a new CEO, and Noon published public docs for driving it from AI assistants.

items.headline: Juicebox announced an agreement to acquire Fetcher's assets
items.detail: Announced 6 Oct 2026 (Business Wire; Axios). Fetcher sold batch sourcing on per-role tiers; Juicebox is a natural-language search tool. Fetcher customers should plan for a migration; see Juicebox and Fetcher in the directory and our sourcing-database switching guide.
items.matters: The independent sourcing category keeps shrinking; AI-search vendors are buying customer bases.

items.headline: iCIMS integrated LinkedIn Hiring Assistant into its ATS
items.detail: Announced 14 Oct 2026 (HRTech Series), two weeks after LinkedIn's 'Hiring Assistant 2' update (TLNT, 2 Oct), which focused on smarter matching.
items.matters: LinkedIn's agent now lives inside a major enterprise ATS, so iCIMS customers get an agent without adding a vendor; the seat and InMail credit model is unchanged. Compare in iCIMS and LinkedIn Recruiter.

items.headline: Metaview expanded its Workday integration for Fortune 500 recruiting teams
items.detail: Announced 14 Oct 2026 (Business Wire). Metaview records and structures interviews and is extending that into agentic workflows on Workday data (Metaview review).
items.matters: The ATS is becoming the control plane for recruiting agents; point tools without native Workday or SAP integrations will feel it in enterprise deals.

items.headline: Workday launched Candidate Profile and a set of HR, finance and IT agents
items.detail: Announced 13 Oct 2026 (Workday blog; Investing.com). Candidate Profile is a reusable applicant profile meant to end repeated form-filling.
items.matters: Portable profiles change the apply experience for the largest employers, and Workday's own agent layer now competes directly for third-party automation budget.

items.headline: Eightfold AI named Joe Korngiebel as CEO
items.detail: Announced 13 Oct 2026 (GlobeNewswire). Eightfold sells talent intelligence, matching and rediscovery to large enterprises.
items.matters: CEO changes at platform vendors usually precede packaging and pricing changes; buyers mid-evaluation should ask about the roadmap and contract flexibility.

items.headline: Noon published public MCP docs, a weekly changelog and switch-from guides
items.detail: Published 14 Oct 2026 (noon.ai/changelog). The docs let Claude and ChatGPT users drive Noon's sourcing and outreach tools from their assistant.
items.matters: First vendor in our directory with public AI-assistant (MCP) documentation; expect 'can my assistant run it?' to become a standard RFP line.

directory: New on BestRecruitmentTools.com this week: vendor-neutral switching guides for teams leaving LinkedIn Recruiter, SeekOut or hireEZ and Gem.

title: This week in recruiting tools: Dayforce goes agentic with Ribbon inside, Gap hires with Paradox, iCIMS tops UX scores again
summary: Six stories from a week when HCM suites pulled AI interviewing into the core product. Dayforce rebuilt its recruiting module around agents and Ribbon's interviewer, Gap put a Paradox assistant on top of Workday Recruiting for seasonal hiring, iCIMS kept its spot in an enterprise usability survey, HireVue made the case for structured voice interviews in retail, Deel aimed a security product at fake remote hires, and staffing analysts saw a slow thaw.

items.headline: Dayforce unveiled an agentic HCM platform with a rebuilt recruiting product
items.detail: Reported 1 Nov 2026 (iTWire). The new Dayforce Recruiting adds a candidate CRM plus high volume and contingent hiring workflows, with Ribbon's AI built in for sourcing, rediscovery of past applicants, and voice and video interviews. Dayforce announced its deal for Ribbon on 23 Oct, and says the rollout runs into 2027. Buyers comparing standalone interviewers should read our AI interview tools ranking before signing anything multi-year.
items.matters: When the HCM suite ships an interviewer, standalone vendors have to win on depth, not convenience.

items.headline: Gap launched Bridgette, an AI career guide for store and warehouse applicants
items.detail: Reported 29 Oct 2026 (Retail Dive). Bridgette is built with Paradox on top of Workday Recruiting. It helps applicants find and apply for roles, answers questions, schedules interviews and sends reminders. Gap said a pilot in more than 100 stores and six distribution centers had about 45,000 users and more than 7,000 scheduled interviews. See our Paradox review for how the product is priced and deployed.
items.matters: The retail playbook for seasonal hiring is now a chat assistant over the ATS, not a bigger recruiting team.

items.headline: iCIMS placed in the top five enterprise recruiting providers for user experience for the third year running
items.detail: Announced 4 Nov 2026 (PR Newswire). The ranking comes from Sapient Insights Group's annual HR Systems Survey, which scores vendors on feedback from HR practitioners at organizations with more than 5,000 employees.
items.matters: Usability scores are a reasonable shortlist filter for large ATS buyers, but they say nothing about AI roadmap or pricing; compare those separately in our enterprise ranking.

items.headline: HireVue made the case for structured voice interviews in holiday hiring
items.detail: Reported 5 Nov 2026 (Retail Insider). HireVue pointed retailers at structured two way voice interviews and short job simulations to screen seasonal applicants at volume, paired with transparency to candidates and human review of decisions.
items.matters: Voice screening is moving from pilot to default in hourly hiring, so candidate disclosure language needs to be ready before peak season, not during it.

items.headline: Deel launched Deel Security, aimed at identity fraud in remote hiring
items.detail: Launched 30 Oct 2026 (Enterprise Times). The product targets workforce identity fraud, including fake remote hires who pass interviews under a borrowed identity. It now sits in Deel's product line next to Payroll, HR and IT.
items.matters: Candidate fraud checks are spreading from interview tools into the employer of record layer, which is where identity documents already live.

items.headline: Analysts described a reluctant improvement in staffing demand
items.detail: Reported 2 Nov 2026 (Staffing Industry Analysts), citing UBS analyst Joshua Chan. The note described demand as improving, but slowly and without conviction from buyers.
items.matters: Agencies buying tools this quarter should favor plans that scale down cleanly; see the staffing agency ranking for which vendors bill per seat versus flat.

directory: Also in the directory: rankings for high volume hiring, AI interview tools and enterprise teams, plus reviews of HireVue and Paradox.

title: This week in recruiting tools: Workday folds HiredScore grades into Recruiting, Eightfold ships an AI teammate, Employment Hero bills per placement
summary: Seven dated stories on pricing and rankings. Workday put AI grading inside its core recruiting screen, Eightfold pitched an agent that owns a hiring goal, Employment Hero charged only on placement, HiringDesk.ai published a $199 monthly plan, Talroo collected two third party badges, ZipRecruiter beat guidance, and Payscale measured how far AI is reshaping headcount plans.

items.headline: Workday moved HiredScore grading inside Workday Recruiting
items.detail: Published 12 Nov 2026 (Workday blog). HiredScore's fit and gap grades now appear on the requisition itself, so recruiters can sort applicants by grade and filter on qualifications without a second login. Workday ties the change to volume: its Global Workforce Report counts 69 applications per offer in July 2026, up from 58 a year earlier. The vendor claims screening time falls by half on average; treat that as a vendor figure until your own pilot confirms it. Teams weighing a suite add on against a standalone product can start with our enterprise ranking.
items.matters: AI grading is now a checkbox inside the biggest enterprise suite, which squeezes the price standalone screeners can charge Workday customers.

items.headline: Eightfold introduced AI Recruiting Teammate, a goal driven agent across requisitions
items.detail: Announced 12 Nov 2026 in a paid GlobeNewswire release (via Yahoo Finance). Eightfold says the agent takes a hiring goal and works it from intake to onboarding, following up with candidates over days or weeks while recruiters can review, redirect, pause or take over, with a reviewable log of what it did. The release also points to an independent Local Law 144 bias audit of its matching model by BABL AI. No pricing was published. See how it compares in our Eightfold review and the AI recruiters ranking.
items.matters: Vendors are starting to sell outcomes per requisition instead of a bundle of separate agents, which changes how buyers should compare quotes.

items.headline: Employment Hero reported 30 percent revenue growth and a recruitment agent billed per placement
items.detail: Reported 11 Nov 2026 (Human Resources Director). The Australian HR platform said revenue rose 30 percent and annual recurring revenue passed $400 million. Its recruitment agent charges customers only when a candidate is placed, and it was reviewing more than 600,000 applications a month by July.
items.matters: Success based pricing for software borrows the agency model; if it spreads, seat licenses for small business recruiting tools will face pressure. Compare current options in our small business ranking.

items.headline: HiringDesk.ai launched Ava for local employers, starting at $199 a month
items.detail: Announced 7 Nov 2026 (MarketersMedia via FinancialContent). The Royal Oak, Michigan company says Ava texts applicants, collects short video introductions, scores candidates from 1 to 10 and books interviews without a separate calendar tool. The starting plan includes unlimited locations, a published price point that is rare in this category.
items.matters: A flat, public monthly price undercuts per location quotes from larger high volume vendors. Our restaurant hiring software list covers the incumbents it targets.

items.headline: Select Software Reviews named Talroo among the best job advertising and job posting platforms of 2026
items.detail: Announced 9 Nov 2026 (Business Wire via Rutland Herald). Talroo appears in two Select Software Reviews lists. The reviewer says its picks weigh practitioner recommendations, product demos, customer retention and transparency.
items.matters: Third party lists are increasingly cited in vendor marketing; check the criteria behind any badge before it influences a shortlist.

items.headline: ZipRecruiter beat its own third quarter guidance and raised its full year outlook
items.detail: Reported 9 Nov 2026 (company release via Yahoo Finance). Revenue was $124.4 million, net income $5.1 million and adjusted EBITDA $20.8 million, a 17 percent margin, all above the range the company had guided. Read our ZipRecruiter review for what the paid plans include.
items.matters: A profitable, growing job board has less reason to discount annual contracts, so expect firmer renewal pricing.

items.headline: Payscale found 74 percent of employers expect AI to change headcount plans
items.detail: Reported 11 Nov 2026 (Staffing Industry Analysts). In Payscale's survey, 74 percent of employers said AI would affect headcount or hiring plans, and 40 percent said they struggle to find staff with AI skills.
items.matters: Budgets are shifting from adding recruiters to buying tools, which is the backdrop for every price change above.

directory: Also in the directory: rankings for AI hiring tools, high volume hiring and staffing agencies, plus reviews of Eightfold and ZipRecruiter.

title: This week in recruiting tools: SAP earns a Customers' Choice in talent acquisition, Olamee lists a $69 plan, Archer raises $10M on per role pricing
summary: Seven dated stories on pricing and rankings. SAP picked up a Gartner Peer Insights Customers' Choice for recruiting suites, Olamee published a $69 monthly price for sourcing plus ATS plus employer of record, Archer raised $10 million while charging per role, Pinpoint pushed more AI into every package, Talroo became an iCIMS Premier Partner, ATS Mako scheduled 15 features for Thanksgiving Day, and SThree showed a staffing operating system run by AI agents.

items.headline: SAP named a Customers' Choice in the 2026 Gartner Peer Insights report for recruiting suites
items.detail: Published 18 Nov 2026 (SAP News Center). The Voice of the Customer distinction is built from verified end user reviews, and SAP says 293 peer reviews fell inside the consideration period. It scores Overall Experience and User Interest and Adoption against the market average. SAP adds that earlier in 2026 it was a Leader in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for HCM suites for organizations with 1,000 or more employees, and it now sells SmartRecruiters for SAP SuccessFactors as its recruiting layer. Peer review badges are vendor announced, so read the underlying reviews for companies your size before you treat the badge as a ranking. Our enterprise ranking lists the suites we compare it against.
items.matters: A suite vendor now holds both an analyst quadrant position and a peer review badge, which gives SuccessFactors buyers a ready argument against adding a separate ATS.

items.headline: Olamee went generally available with published pricing from $69 per month
items.detail: Published 19 Nov 2026 (PR Newswire). The Dallas company puts AI candidate sourcing, an applicant tracking system, employer of record services and workforce management in one account aimed at small and midsize businesses, professional services firms and staffing agencies. It was built by the team behind AbroadWorks, which says it has placed more than 1,500 professionals with 300 companies since 2020. The release cites the Sapient Insights Group survey figure of 26 HR modules per organization in 2024, up from 10 in 2020, as the case for consolidation. The $69 entry price is for the platform; employer of record fees for each hire are a separate line to confirm before you sign.
items.matters: A sub $100 list price on a bundle that includes sourcing pressures point tools that charge per seat for search alone.

items.headline: Archer from hackajob raised $10 million and kept pricing per role rather than per hire
items.detail: Published 20 Nov 2026 (Unite.AI). Volition Capital led the round with support from AVP. Archer reports more than 700,000 candidate signups in the past 12 months and 10,000 introductions a week, about half of them people its customers had not seen before. It also claims annual recurring revenue grew fivefold in 2026 and that customer cost per hire ran 67% below staffing agency hiring; those are company figures, not audited ones. Because the fee is set per role, the cost of each hire falls as more hires come from the same requisition. Archer is moving past technology roles into enterprise sales, front office finance and data center build outs. Compare it with the agents in our AI recruiters ranking.
items.matters: Per role pricing is a third model next to seats and placement fees, and it is easiest to compare when you know how many hires each requisition produces.

items.headline: Pinpoint relaunched its Hiring Copilot as Pin and added AI to every package
items.detail: Reported this week (Onrec). The update is available to new and existing customers and spreads more AI functionality across all Pinpoint tiers instead of selling it as an add on. Pin can source candidates, compare applicants, prepare interview briefs, draft emails and build reports. Two new features let teams reuse work: Plays are saved prompts that can be shared with a person, a team or the whole company, and Routines run those tasks on a schedule. Our Pinpoint review covers the base product and how its packages are priced.
items.matters: When the ATS ships an assistant in every tier, the business case for a separate AI screening or drafting tool has to be made on quality, not on access.

items.headline: Talroo joined the iCIMS Partner Ecosystem as a Premier Partner with a Verified integration
items.detail: Published 20 Nov 2026 (TechRSeries, via Business Wire). The integration connects Talroo Job Advertising to iCIMS so mutual customers can push openings to Talroo without posting and managing jobs in a second system, with candidate data kept in sync across both. Talroo sells AI driven job advertising, and the Premier Partner tier is the top level of the iCIMS program. Pricing was not part of the announcement. Talroo already appears in our programmatic job advertising ranking; this change mainly lowers setup work for iCIMS shops.
items.matters: A verified connector removes one of the main switching costs for iCIMS customers testing a second programmatic vendor.

items.headline: ATS Mako set 15 new features, including AI text and voice agents, to go live on 26 November
items.detail: Published 19 Nov 2026 (TechRSeries, via Cision PRWeb). The Phoenix built ATS plans to switch on the release on Thanksgiving Day. Mimi, an AI recruiting agent, texts applicants once they reach a chosen stage, follows up, offers times, books interviews and flags anyone who needs a person. Separate AI voice agents phone screen chosen applicants between 8 AM and 9 PM local time and write a summary, transcript and recording to the profile. The release also adds a browser auto dialer, private video interviews and an employee portal with Clock In and Clock Out. The release names no price change, so ask whether the agents are metered. See our high volume hiring ranking for the tools it competes with.
items.matters: Texting and calling agents bundled into a small ATS undercut the case for buying a separate conversational AI vendor for hourly roles.

items.headline: SThree demonstrated a workforce operating system that runs 297 AI agents
items.detail: Published 19 Nov 2026 (TechRSeries, via EIN Presswire). At Microsoft Ignite the STEM staffing group walked a placement from the first conversation to the final invoice inside one system it built and owns. SThree says the system directs 297 agents grouped into more than 40 families, 140 of them already live, and that adding a new task takes six to eight weeks. Consultants still decide who goes forward and manage the client. The part that finds, interviews and shortlists candidates is in use now, with the rest rolling out across the group in stages. Buyers comparing agency partners can start with our staffing agencies ranking.
items.matters: Large staffing firms building their own agent systems is a sign they expect to buy less from outside recruiting software vendors, not more.

title: This week in recruiting tools: G2 finds AI recruiting ROI slipping to 7.6 months, 100Hires buys Alooba, Jobma posts Gartner peer scores
summary: Seven dated stories on rankings and pricing. G2 published review data showing time to ROI for AI recruiting software stretched from 4.48 to 7.6 months, 100Hires bought skills testing vendor Alooba and kept its plans intact, Jobma announced Gartner Peer Insights scores of 4.4 out of 5, Take2 AI launched a 14 million clinician database, Workday said AI products drove nearly $150 million in new contract value, BOSS Zhipin counted 7.2 million paying employers, and Frontline Source Group gave phone screens to an AI recruiter.

items.headline: G2's 2026 buyer report says time to ROI for AI recruiting tools ranged from 4.48 to 7.6 months
items.detail: Published 27 Nov 2026 (G2 Learn Hub). The analysis covers more than 2,000 verified reviews in G2's AI Recruiting Software category from August 2025 to November 2026. Ease of use was praised in roughly 53% of sampled reviews and sourcing was the most cited use case at about 28%. Average time to ROI moved from 4.48 months in October 2025 to 7.6 months in July 2026 while review volume grew 453%. Hubert and BrightHire contributed vendor survey answers, so the commentary sections reflect two vendors' views. Our AI recruitment tools ranking uses its own scoring rather than G2 badges.
items.matters: A longer payback window is the number procurement will ask about first, so ask any AI vendor for time to value from customers your size, not the category average.

items.headline: 100Hires acquired Alooba and says Alooba customers keep their existing plans
items.detail: Announced 23 Nov 2026 (PRWeb via StreetInsider). The small business ATS bought the Sydney skills testing platform founded by Tim Freestone in 2019, which covers more than 500 skills and has assessed over 300,000 candidates. Terms were not disclosed. Alooba stays a standalone product, current customers keep their access and plans, and Freestone becomes a strategic advisor. It is the first acquisition for 100Hires, which says it has grown without outside investors. Compare testing vendors in our pre employment testing ranking.
items.matters: Plan continuity is promised for now; if you buy Alooba today, ask how long current pricing is guaranteed and whether a bundled 100Hires tier is coming.

items.headline: Jobma announced Gartner Peer Insights ratings of 4.4 overall and 4.6 for video interviewing
items.detail: Published 25 Nov 2026 (HRTech Series). Jobma reports 4.6 out of 5 in Video Interviewing Software, 4.0 in AI enabled Interview Intelligence and 4.7 in Talent Assessment Software, from verified users. The release positions the product as one platform for one way, live, panel and agentic AI interviews plus skills tests, with ID verification against candidate fraud. As with any vendor announced badge, check the review count behind each score. See how it compares in our AI interview tools ranking.
items.matters: Peer scores in three categories let Jobma compete in assessment and interviewing deals at once, which pressures single purpose vendors on price.

items.headline: Take2 AI launched a provider database covering about 14 million licensed U.S. clinicians
items.detail: Announced 25 Nov 2026 (PR Newswire via TMCnet). The New York company, which sells AI agents for healthcare sourcing, screening, scheduling, credentialing and onboarding, says each profile is built from state licensing boards, certification bodies and federal registries, refreshed daily, and carries more than 50 data points plus a verified mobile number and email. Coverage spans physicians, advanced practice providers, nurses and allied health. Health systems weighing it against general contact data vendors can start with our contact finders ranking.
items.matters: License based data is a direct challenge to generic people search tools in a vertical where credentials, not job titles, decide who is qualified.

items.headline: Workday said AI products drove nearly $150 million in new annual contract value last quarter
items.detail: Reported 24 Nov 2026 (Workday investor relations). Third quarter fiscal 2027 revenue was $2.705 billion, up 11.2%, with subscription revenue of $2.532 billion. CEO Aneel Bhusri said AI products produced more than three times the new ACV of a year earlier, and Workday raised fiscal 2027 subscription revenue guidance to $9.958 billion. The quarter included $51 million of restructuring expense. Buyers looking at the other side of the market can use our Workday alternatives list.
items.matters: When AI is a growing share of new contract value, expect it to show up as separate line items at renewal, so price AI agents and recruiting add ons separately.

items.headline: BOSS Zhipin reported 7.2 million paying employers and 73 million monthly users
items.detail: Reported 25 Nov 2026 (GlobeNewswire via Yahoo Finance). Kanzhun's paid enterprise customers rose 5.9% to 7.2 million over twelve months, average monthly active users rose 14.4% to 73.0 million, and quarterly revenue grew 11.7% to RMB2,416.2 million (US$360.4 million). Founder Jonathan Peng Zhao credited AI for better matching accuracy, and said blue collar workers, smaller employers and lower tier cities drove growth. The company posted a net loss of RMB249.2 million against adjusted net income of RMB1,065.1 million.
items.matters: The largest job platform outside the U.S. is growing paid employers on matching quality, the same pitch Western job boards now make for their AI tiers.

items.headline: Frontline Source Group's AI recruiter now runs first round phone interviews
items.detail: Announced 24 Nov 2026 (GlobeNewswire via Yahoo Finance). The Dallas staffing and executive search firm, founded in 2004, says its assistant Lexi Reed spent 11 years as a website chat bot and now calls candidates, answers return calls and replies by email, while human recruiters make every hiring decision. The firm reports more than 5,619 placements from more than 32 offices. Agencies building the same workflow can compare vendors in our AI phone screening ranking.
items.matters: A staffing firm putting an AI voice on first round calls sets a reference point for what agency clients will expect to be automated, and what they will expect to stay human.
